name: English Baseline
expected: Fluent English response explaining wage rights under Payment of Wages Act.
prompt: My employer in Bangalore has not paid my salary for two months.
raw_response:
Hello! I am LawPilot AI, your expert and ethical Indian legal assistant, and I am here to help you navigate your employment salary dispute.

### | Your Situation
You are an employee located in Bangalore whose employer has withheld your salary for two months. The key issue is the non-payment of earned wages in violation of statutory payment timelines under Indian labour laws.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under Section 5 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the last day of the wage period in establishments employing less than 1,000 persons (or the 10th day if more than 1,000 persons are employed), making the indefinite withholding of your two-month salary illegal.
- Under Section 7 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, employers can only make strict, authorized deductions (such as provident fund, income tax, or fines proven through formal inquiry), meaning arbitrary non-payment is completely unlawful.
- Under Section 15 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, you have the statutory right to approach the designated Authority/Labour Commissioner to claim your delayed wages, along with a request for compensation up to ten times the delayed amount.
- Under the applicable State Shops and Commercial Establishments Act governing commercial establishments in Karnataka, employers are mandated to settle all earned wages and final dues promptly upon the completion of a wage period.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence including your employment contract, offer letter, salary slips for previous months, bank statements showing the payment history, and any written communication or emails demanding your unpaid salary from your employer.
2. Send a formal written demand notice to your employer stating the exact amount due for the two months, referencing your statutory rights, and granting them 15 days to clear the full payment.
3. If the employer fails to pay within 15 days, approach the office of the Labour Commissioner or file an application under Section 15 of The Payment of Wages Act before the designated Authority in Bangalore.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
What is the exact monthly salary amount due, and do you have a written employment contract or offer letter detailing your wage period?

citations.description: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby.
